correctness.evidence: Clean-room Catalan-recursive enumeration through n=10 reproduced Catalan totals, verified the stated Dyck map object-by-object, and reproduced exactly the n=9 and n=10 LIS histograms and Narayana formula.

originality.evidence: Deutsch, Hildebrand and Wilf, arXiv:math/0304126 (2003), Section 2 equation (2.1), citing Reifegerste, states for arbitrary n that the number of 231-avoiding permutations with LIS exactly k is (1/n) C(n,k) C(n,k-1). The record's n=9 and n=10 tables are direct specializations.

value.evidence: After subtracting the known all-n exact enumeration, the surviving contribution is an exhaustive replay/certificate for two parameter values. It supplies useful reproducibility but no new mathematical regime, theorem, or substantive improvement sufficient for this campaign's scientific-value bar.

literature.title: Longest increasing subsequences in pattern-restricted permutations
literature.authors: Emeric Deutsch; A. J. Hildebrand; Herbert S. Wilf
literature.coverage: Exact all-n formula e(n,k)=(1/n) binom(n,k) binom(n,k-1) for 231-avoiding permutations.

repair.reason: Narrowing to a finite replay certificate is accurate but does not create a scientifically valuable mathematical result after the exact all-n formula is acknowledged.

final_reason: Correct finite computation, but decisive prior-art coverage defeats originality and leaves no substantive residual scientific value.
